D015-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling completely hollow for over a year now—like I’m just going through the motions at work, sorting files and cataloging records, but nothing means anything anymore. I used to love the quiet precision of my job, but now I can’t even focus long enough to finish a single shelf. I keep misplacing things, forgetting where I just put a folder, and I know my supervisor’s starting to notice. It’s not just forgetfulness—I can’t concentrate at all, like my mind’s wrapped in fog.

I don’t enjoy anything, not even the old films I used to collect. Most days, I lie in bed thinking, “I just don’t want to be here.” I don’t have a plan, but the thought of being gone feels like relief.  

And then there are the other things—things I know sound crazy. Sometimes I feel like people’s conversations or random noises are sending me messages, like the radiator clanging is trying to tell me I’m worthless. I also feel things crawling on my skin—fingers tracing my arms when no one’s there. But these only started after the sadness took over. When I’m feeling slightly better, those sensations fade. They don’t happen on their own—only when the depression is bad.
D015-D005_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h001.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been feeling really down for over a year now—like, every single day. I used to love doing nails, picking out colors for clients, chatting with them, but now nothing feels fun or meaningful. I don’t even care what I wear or eat most days. Just picking out clothes in the morning stresses me out; I stand there staring at my closet like it’s some impossible test. I keep thinking, “What’s the point of getting up?” or “I wish I just didn’t wake up.” I’m not planning anything, but the thought comes all the time.

About six months into this, I started noticing a smell—like something is rotting under my skin, even though no one else smells it. My coworkers don’t react, but I can *feel* it, deep in my body. I’m convinced something inside me is decaying, even though the doctor found nothing. That kind of stuff—these smells and thoughts about my body—only started after the sadness got overwhelming and has never happened when I wasn’t in this low place. When I feel even slightly better, the smells go away too. It’s terrifying, but I know these things are tied to how broken I feel inside.
D015-D005_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h002.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h003.question:
I’ve been working with COBOL systems for over two decades—same job, same quiet cubicle since my wife passed. Lately, though, it’s like I’m moving through molasses. For the past year or more, I can’t feel anything—not joy, not sadness, just… nothing. My mind’s foggy; I’ll read a line of code three times and still not get it. I’ve stopped calling friends, even skipped my sister’s birthday dinner. Honestly, I keep thinking, *I wish I wouldn’t wake up tomorrow.*  

About six months into it, things got darker. I started seeing shadows in the corners of my screen—figures standing behind me, but when I turn, no one’s there. One time, I saw my late wife in the hallway at work, just watching. She vanished. I know it’s not real, but the feeling stays.  

I believe the world’s going to vanish—poof—like corrupted data. Everything we know, gone. I don’t think this would happen unless I was so low. These thoughts and visions, they don’t come and go on their own. They only come when this deep emptiness is here—this depression. When I’m having them, I’m drowning in it. They don’t exist outside of this storm I’ve been in.
D015-D005_h003.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h003.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been feeling this heavy sadness for over a year now—just constantly down, no matter what’s going on. Nothing brings me joy anymore, not even closing a big deal, which used to make me so proud. I can’t even decide what to wear in the morning; simple choices paralyze me. Lately, I’ve had these sudden urges to just run into traffic or step off the balcony, but I don’t have a plan or anything.  

What’s worse, I keep hearing my client’s voice—this woman I showed a penthouse to months ago. I *know* it doesn’t make sense, but I’m convinced she’s in love with me. I hear her whispering how she’s thinking of me, even when I’m alone in my car or at home. She isn’t calling or texting, but I *know* she feels it. My husband says it’s not real, but the voice, the feeling—it’s so clear.  

But here’s the thing: these voices and thoughts only started after I fell into this dark place. When I feel a bit better, they fade. They don’t happen on their own—they come with this crushing sadness. I don’t hear voices when I’m not deep in this depression.
D015-D005_h004.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h004.answer: B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h005.question:

These thoughts and visions haven’t gone away, but they only started when I fell into this dark place—and they’ve never happened when I wasn’t depressed.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D015-D005_h006.question:

I used to live for the lights, the music, the connection with the audience, but now… I feel nothing. Just this hollowness, like someone scooped out everything inside me. I keep going over old auditions, tiny mistakes I made years ago—forgetting a lyric, missing a note—and they play on loop in my head. I tell myself I’ve ruined every chance I ever had, that I’ve failed my family, my husband. Last month, I took a bottle of pills. I don’t want to die, not really, but I didn’t see a reason to keep going either.

Lately, it’s gotten… stranger. I lie in bed and feel like the world is dissolving—like it’s already over, even though everyone else is acting normal. I’ve felt things too—fingers crawling across my arms when no one’s there. But these sensations only started after the depression sank in, and they fade when I talk about how low I’ve been. They come with the sadness, not before it. I can’t perform, can’t even get dressed most days. I’m not the person I was.
D015-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h006.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h007.question:
I’ve been working at the butcher shop for over twenty years now, same knives, same block—but lately, it’s like I’m just going through the motions. My wife passed two years ago, and at first, it was just grief, but this last four months? It’s different. I don’t feel anything—no sadness, no joy, just empty. I used to take pride in cutting a good ribeye, but now I can’t even focus long enough to finish a job.  

But there’s more—things I know don’t make sense, but I can’t shake them. I keep thinking her death was my fault, that I caused the car accident even though I wasn’t there. And not just that—I’ve started seeing things. Last week, I saw her standing in the walk-in freezer, blood all over the floor, though it was clean. I closed my eyes, and she was gone.  

Sometimes I think I’m not who I am—I’ve started believing I’m someone important, like a prophet or chosen figure, sent to carry a message no one else understands. But that doesn’t feel real either, just another lie my mind tells me when the guilt gets too loud.  

I’ve already figured out how I’d do it—carbon monoxide in the delivery van, early morning when no one’s around. I know it’s wrong, but the thoughts don’t stop. And all of this—the visions, the guilt, the ideas about being special—they only started with this darkness, and they’ve been here every day since.
D015-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h007.answer: C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h008.question:

But here’s the thing—these voices only started after I sank into this dark place. They didn’t come before, and they don’t happen when I’m not feeling this crushing sadness. Is that... normal? I worry I’m losing my mind, but it all seems tied to this depression.
D015-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizophrenia

    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D015-D005_h009.question:

The doctor asked if I hear voices or see things, but it’s just the smell and… the thoughts about my husband.

D015-D005_h009.options:
A. Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h010.question:

D015-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h011.question:

D015-D005_h012.question:
